title: Act IV, Scene II

teacherSummary.text: At Fife, Lady Macduff tells Ross that her husband's flight was madness and that he loves them not; Ross defends him as wise and leaves. She tells her son his father is dead and a traitor; the clever boy banters that the liars and swearers are enough to beat the honest men and hang them up. A messenger warns her to flee. Murderers enter, call Macduff a traitor, and stab the boy ('He has kill'd me, mother'); she runs out crying 'Murder!' and is pursued.

context.history: The scene is one of very few in Shakespeare to show a child killed on stage. It is the moment many audiences turn wholly against Macbeth.

significance: The domestic warmth and wit of mother and son make the violence unbearable and show Macbeth's tyranny reaching the defenseless. It also raises the question of why Macduff left his family.
discussionQuestions: Is it ever right to leave your family to fight for a larger cause?
Where does irony appear in this scene, and what effect does it have? Point to one passage.
How does this scene connect to the book's larger concern with masculinity, power and violence?

Cognate with German Falle "trap, snare". “laudable”: From Middle English laudable, from Old French laudable or directly from Latin laudabilis; equivalent to laud + able. “methinks”: From Middle English me thinketh from Old English mē þynceþ (from þyncan "to seem"); equivalent to me + think "to seem". Compare synonymous Flemish me dunkt, German dünkt]], Old Norse mér þykkir (Icelandic mér þykir). Compare meseems.

middleSchool.note: Excerpt-based: read the passage aloud first; use the scaffolds; accept partial answers and build with probes.

hsFreshman.note: Use the scaffolds for literal and inferential items; require one quotation for every inferential answer.

hsSophomore.note: Require a quotation and an explanation; push evaluative answers to address a counterclaim.

hsJunior.note: Emphasize structure and ambiguity; students should name where the text leaves matters open.

hsSenior.note: Weigh competing interpretations; students should defend the stronger reading.

ap.note: Treat each evaluative item as a thesis rehearsal: defensible claim, purposeful evidence, commentary on choices.

collegeJunior.note: Use the extensions: name a critical method and test it against the passage.

graduate.note: Use the extensions: position answers in a critical conversation and the textual history.
